parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: Disodium phosphate, $(\text{Na}^+)_2(\text{HPO}_4^{2-})$, reacts with an acid to form monosodium phosphate, $\text{Na}^+(\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-)$.
parts.text:
Identify the ions that are a conjugate acid-base pair in this reaction, using the formulae of the species involved.

conjugate acid conjugate base

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Write two equations to show how a mixture of $(\text{Na}^+)_2(\text{HPO}_4^{2-})$ and $\text{Na}^+(\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-)$ can act as a buffer solution.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text: Identify one inorganic ion that acts as a buffer in blood.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
Compound E is the hydroxide of a Group 2 element. Compound E is a strong alkali.

$2.63\text{ g}$ of E is dissolved in water to make $250\text{ cm}^3$ of solution F. Solution F has a pH of 13.09 at $298\text{ K}$.
parts.text: Show that the concentration of hydroxide ions in solution F is $0.123\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the concentration of compound E in solution F is $0.0615\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Use the concentration given in (ii) to identify compound E.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Compound E is much more soluble than magnesium hydroxide.

A saturated solution of magnesium hydroxide in water has a concentration of $1.40 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ at $298\text{ K}$.

Calculate the solubility product, $K_{\text{sp}}$, of magnesium hydroxide. Include units.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain why compound E is much more soluble than magnesium hydroxide.
